---
title: "What makes up Tampa's mapped bicycle network?"
output: html_document
---

Compare Tampa's bicycle connections by segment count and reported mileage.
The layer includes shared roads, paths, and trails as well as bike lanes.

Install `tampaBayOpenData`, `knitr`, and `rmarkdown`. Knitting retrieves
live data; check provenance for the download time.

**Source:** [City of Tampa Bike Lanes layer and field definitions](https://arcgis.tampagov.net/arcgis/rest/services/OpenData/Transportation/MapServer/0)
and its [ArcGIS item and reuse information](https://tampa.maps.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=d54aac9d4559488fa439e454df5f09ce).

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = TRUE,
                      fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5, out.width = "100%")
library(tampaBayOpenData)
```

## Retrieve data

Retrieve all records rather than a preview. Each row represents a **mapped
line segment**, not a complete bicycle route: a route may cross many segments,
and the layer alone does not establish whether they form a usable connection.

The download includes a provenance record:

- `complete = TRUE` means all records matching this request were returned.
- `integrity` describes the checks used to validate the download.
  `full-manifest` means returned object IDs were checked against the full list
  of IDs requested from the service, rather than just a bounded preview.
- `validation_status = "checked"` identifies a bundled, reviewed package
  entry. It does not certify the accuracy or current condition of every feature.

Unique, nonmissing `OBJECTID` values ensure that each mapped record is counted
once. These checks protect the shares below from a partial or duplicated download;
if they fail, rerun the retrieval and inspect `tbod_provenance(segments)`.
The qualified ID below is supported by this package checkout; older installations
can use the preserved `"bike-lanes"` alias if needed.

```{r retrieve}
segments <- tbod_get_dataset(
  "tampa-bike-lanes",
  fields = c("OBJECTID", "CONN_TYPE", "MILEAGE", "ROADWAY"),
  page_size = 500,
  total_timeout = 120
)
source <- tbod_provenance(segments)
if (!isTRUE(source$complete) ||
    !identical(source$integrity, "full-manifest") ||
    !identical(source$validation_status, "checked") ||
    !isTRUE(nrow(segments) == source$matched_rows) ||
    !isTRUE(nrow(segments) == source$returned_rows)) {
  stop("The download is not a complete, checked full-manifest retrieval. Rerun and inspect its provenance.")
}
required_fields <- c("OBJECTID", "CONN_TYPE", "MILEAGE", "ROADWAY")
if (!all(required_fields %in% names(segments)) ||
    !is.numeric(segments$MILEAGE)) {
  stop("Expected fields or numeric MILEAGE changed. Inspect tbod_dataset_info('tampa-bike-lanes', refresh = TRUE).")
}
if (!nrow(segments)) stop("The live layer is empty; there are no segments to compare. Try again later.")
if (anyNA(segments$OBJECTID) || anyDuplicated(segments$OBJECTID)) {
  stop("Missing or duplicate OBJECTID values would distort counts. Rerun the download before analysis.")
}

# A vertical table keeps provenance readable on a narrow article page.
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  item = c("Publisher", "Retrieved at (UTC)", "Matched rows", "Returned rows",
           "Complete", "Integrity", "Validation status"),
  value = c(source$publisher,
            format(source$retrieved_at, tz = "UTC", usetz = TRUE),
            source$matched_rows, source$returned_rows,
            source$complete, source$integrity, source$validation_status)
), col.names = c("Download detail", "Value"))
knitr::kable(utils::head(segments, 5))
```

Connection labels come from the coded-value **domain**: the publisher's lookup
from stored `CONN_TYPE` codes to readable labels. The next chunk finds that field
in the metadata returned with this download and displays the lookup. Without it,
we cannot verify what the codes mean, so the tutorial stops rather than guessing.

```{r field-definitions}
connection_fields <- Filter(
  function(field) identical(field$name, "CONN_TYPE"), source$field_schema
)
if (length(connection_fields) != 1L) {
  stop("CONN_TYPE metadata is missing or duplicated. Inspect the live layer field definitions before continuing.")
}
codes <- connection_fields[[1]]$domain$codedValues
if (!length(codes) || !all(vapply(codes, function(value) {
  is.character(value$code) && length(value$code) == 1L && !is.na(value$code) &&
    nzchar(value$code) && is.character(value$name) && length(value$name) == 1L &&
    !is.na(value$name) && nzchar(trimws(value$name))
}, logical(1)))) {
  stop("CONN_TYPE has no usable coded-value domain. Review the publisher metadata before assigning families.")
}
code_names <- stats::setNames(
  vapply(codes, function(value) trimws(as.character(value$name)), character(1)),
  vapply(codes, function(value) as.character(value$code), character(1))
)
if (anyDuplicated(names(code_names))) {
  stop("The CONN_TYPE domain contains duplicate codes. Review its definitions before analysis.")
}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  code = names(code_names), publisher_label = unname(code_names)
))
```

## Check mileage

`MILEAGE` is the publisher's reported mileage attribute (field alias `Mileage`),
not a length calculated here from geometry. The service's map-coordinate unit is
meters; it is not the unit of this separate attribute. The field metadata does
not document its calculation method, precision, or whether overlaps are removed.
We treat the attribute as reported miles, not independently measured route miles.

Missing mileage is **unknown, not zero**: those records remain in segment counts
but are excluded from mileage sums. A reported zero remains a known zero; its
cause is not explained by the field metadata. The table makes both visible.
Negative or infinite values invalidate the comparison and stop the analysis.

The code below counts missing values, finds codes absent from the live lookup,
and summarizes each publisher category without dropping unclassified records.

```{r quality}
connection_code <- as.character(segments$CONN_TYPE)
connection_code[is.na(connection_code) | !nzchar(trimws(connection_code))] <-
  "(missing)"
unknown_codes <- setdiff(unique(connection_code),
                         c(names(code_names), "(missing)"))
roadway <- trimws(as.character(segments$ROADWAY))
roadway[is.na(roadway)] <- ""

quality <- data.frame(
  check = c("Returned segments", "Missing connection code",
            "Codes absent from current metadata", "Missing reported mileage",
            "Zero reported mileage", "Negative reported mileage",
            "Blank or N/A roadway label"),
  value = c(nrow(segments), sum(connection_code == "(missing)"),
            length(unknown_codes), sum(is.na(segments$MILEAGE)),
            sum(segments$MILEAGE == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            sum(segments$MILEAGE < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            sum(toupper(roadway) %in% c("", "NA", "N/A")))
)
knitr::kable(quality, col.names = c("Check", "Count"))
if (length(unknown_codes)) {
  warning("Codes absent from current metadata: ", paste(unknown_codes, collapse = ", "),
          ". These records remain in Other or new code.")
}
if (any(connection_code == "(missing)")) {
  warning("Missing CONN_TYPE values remain in Other or new code.")
}
if (anyNA(segments$MILEAGE)) {
  warning("Missing MILEAGE values are excluded from mileage sums, but their segments remain in counts.")
}
if (any(!is.finite(segments$MILEAGE) & !is.na(segments$MILEAGE))) {
  stop("Non-finite MILEAGE values need publisher review before aggregation.")
}
if (any(segments$MILEAGE < 0, na.rm = TRUE)) {
  stop("Negative MILEAGE values need publisher review before aggregation; do not remove them silently.")
}

class_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  split(seq_len(nrow(segments)), connection_code),
  function(rows) {
    code <- connection_code[rows[1]]
    label <- unname(code_names[code])
    if (is.na(label)) label <- paste("Unclassified:", code)
    data.frame(
      code = code, publisher_label = label,
      segments = length(rows),
      reported_miles = sum(segments$MILEAGE[rows], na.rm = TRUE),
      missing_mileage = sum(is.na(segments$MILEAGE[rows])),
      zero_mile_segments = sum(segments$MILEAGE[rows] == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  }
))
class_summary <- class_summary[order(-class_summary$reported_miles), ]
rownames(class_summary) <- NULL
knitr::kable(class_summary, digits = 2,
             col.names = c("Code", "Publisher category", "Segments", "Reported miles",
                           "Missing mileage", "Zero-mileage segments"))
```

## Compare shares

These are **tutorial-defined analytical groupings**, not official City of Tampa
classifications. The displayed publisher labels remain the authoritative meanings
of the individual codes. We combine the three shared-roadway stress categories;
the two bike-lane categories; and multi-use paths with trails. Difficult connections,
neighborhood greenways, and sidewalk connections stay in *Other connections*:
this broad residual group makes no claim that they share a design or stress level.
In particular, a neighborhood greenway is not reclassified as a dedicated lane.

The expected labels below were checked against the publisher's live `BikeLaneType`
domain. Each knit compares those meanings again. A new code, a removed definition,
or a changed label triggers a warning and stays in *Other or new code* until
reviewed. Whitespace around publisher labels does not change their meaning.

```{r family-comparison, fig.height=6, fig.alt="Grouped horizontal bars compare segment and reported mileage shares for each tutorial-defined connection family on a 0 to 100 percent scale."}
expected_labels <- c(
  SR_LT_LS = "Shared Roadway (Low Stress)",
  SR_MHT_LS = "Shared Roadway (Moderate Stress)",
  SR_LT_HS = "Shared Roadway (High Stress)",
  BL_HT_HS = "Bike Lane (High Stress)",
  SBL_LT_LS = "Bike Lane (Separated and/or Low Stress)",
  MUP = "Multi-Use Path", TR = "Trail", DC = "Difficult Connection",
  NG = "Neighborhood Greenway", SC = "Sidewalk Connection"
)
verified_codes <- names(expected_labels)[
  !is.na(code_names[names(expected_labels)]) &
    code_names[names(expected_labels)] == expected_labels
]
review_codes <- union(setdiff(names(expected_labels), verified_codes),
                      setdiff(names(code_names), names(expected_labels)))
if (length(review_codes)) {
  warning("Review new, missing, or changed CONN_TYPE definitions: ",
          paste(review_codes, collapse = ", "),
          ". Affected records remain in Other or new code.")
}
family_by_code <- c(
  SR_LT_LS = "Shared roadway", SR_MHT_LS = "Shared roadway",
  SR_LT_HS = "Shared roadway",
  BL_HT_HS = "Bike-lane categories", SBL_LT_LS = "Bike-lane categories",
  MUP = "Paths and trails", TR = "Paths and trails",
  DC = "Other connections", NG = "Other connections",
  SC = "Other connections"
)
family_by_code <- family_by_code[verified_codes]
family_name <- unname(family_by_code[connection_code])
family_name[is.na(family_name)] <- "Other or new code"
family <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(seq_len(nrow(segments)), family_name),
  function(rows) data.frame(
    family = family_name[rows[1]], segments = length(rows),
    reported_miles = sum(segments$MILEAGE[rows], na.rm = TRUE)
  )
))
rownames(family) <- NULL
total_miles <- sum(segments$MILEAGE, na.rm = TRUE)
if (total_miles <= 0) {
  stop("Total observed MILEAGE is zero or all mileage is missing. Mileage shares are undefined; inspect the quality table and publisher data.")
}
family$segment_share_pct <- 100 * family$segments / nrow(segments)
family$mileage_share_pct <- 100 * family$reported_miles / total_miles
family_order <- c("Shared roadway", "Bike-lane categories",
                  "Paths and trails", "Other connections", "Other or new code")
family <- family[order(match(family$family, family_order)), ]
rownames(family) <- NULL
knitr::kable(family, digits = 2,
             col.names = c("Tutorial family", "Segments", "Reported miles",
                           "Segment share (%)", "Mileage share (%)"))

shares <- rbind("Segments" = family$segment_share_pct,
                "Reported miles" = family$mileage_share_pct)
# Reserve space above the bars for a legend, and left of them for labels.
old_par <- par(mar = c(4.5, 12, 6, 1))
barplot(shares, beside = TRUE, horiz = TRUE, names.arg = family$family,
        las = 1, cex.names = 0.9, col = c("#0072B2", "#E69F00"),
        border = NA, xlim = c(0, 100),
        xlab = "Share of segments or reported mileage (%)")
legend("top", inset = c(0, -0.17), xpd = NA, horiz = TRUE,
       legend = rownames(shares), fill = c("#0072B2", "#E69F00"), bty = "n")
title("Mapped connection mix", line = 4)
par(old_par)
```

The fixed 0 to 100% scale makes both series directly comparable. Segment shares
use all returned rows; mileage shares use only the sum of observed mileage.
Missing mileage can therefore affect the comparison as well as segment length.

## Check zero mileage

Count records with a reported zero by the publisher's individual categories,
not the tutorial families. Long labels wrap onto multiple lines. Zero values
could reflect source-data conventions or unrecorded lengths; this chart cannot
determine why they occur. Missing mileage is excluded from these counts.

```{r zero-mileage, fig.height=7, fig.alt="Horizontal bars count zero-mileage segments by publisher category, with long category labels wrapped."}
zero_classes <- class_summary[class_summary$zero_mile_segments > 0, ]
if (nrow(zero_classes)) {
  zero_classes <- zero_classes[order(zero_classes$zero_mile_segments), ]
  wrapped_labels <- vapply(zero_classes$publisher_label, function(label) {
    paste(strwrap(label, width = 34), collapse = "\n")
  }, character(1))
  old_par <- par(mar = c(4.5, 16, 3, 1))
  barplot(zero_classes$zero_mile_segments, horiz = TRUE,
          names.arg = wrapped_labels, las = 1, cex.names = 0.85, space = 0.6,
          col = "#0072B2", border = NA,
          xlab = "Number of segments with zero reported mileage",
          main = "Zero reported mileage by publisher category")
  par(old_par)
} else {
  cat("No zero-mileage segments in this run.\n")
}

cat(sprintf(
  "Retrieved %s mapped segments with %.2f summed reported miles at %s.\n",
  format(nrow(segments), big.mark = ","), total_miles,
  format(source$retrieved_at, tz = "UTC", usetz = TRUE)
))
```

## What do the results tell us?

```{r interpretation, include=FALSE}
leading_families <- family$family[family$reported_miles == max(family$reported_miles)]
leading_miles <- max(family$reported_miles)
leading_share <- max(family$mileage_share_pct)
share_gap <- abs(family$segment_share_pct - family$mileage_share_pct)
largest_shifts <- family[abs(share_gap - max(share_gap)) < 1e-8, ]
```

**Observed in this retrieval:** **`r paste(leading_families, collapse = " and ")`**
has the most reported mileage (`r sprintf("%.2f", leading_miles)` miles,
`r sprintf("%.1f", leading_share)`% of the observed total; multiple names
indicate a tie). The largest absolute gap between segment share and mileage
share is `r sprintf("%.1f", max(share_gap))` percentage points:

```{r share-gap}
knitr::kable(largest_shifts[, c("family", "segment_share_pct", "mileage_share_pct")],
             digits = 1, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Tutorial family", "Segment share (%)", "Mileage share (%)"))
```

**Interpretation:** Counting segments gives each mapped line one vote; summing
mileage gives longer lines more weight. Splitting one line into smaller records
can change segment counts without changing the underlying mileage. Missing
mileage can also reduce a family's observed mileage share. These are possible
explanations, not evidence of the cause for any particular category.

## Limits

Mapped mileage does not directly measure safety, comfort, connectivity, or
accessibility. Shared roadways and difficult or sidewalk connections are included;
not every mapped connection is protected or dedicated bicycle infrastructure.
Even the separated/low-stress lane label combines alternatives and does not
establish protection for every record. Stress labels are publisher categories,
not an independent safety assessment in this tutorial.

Overlapping segments may count more than once in mileage totals. Unique
`OBJECTID` values prevent repeated records, not overlapping geometry. We have
not assembled routes, tested network continuity, or checked conditions on the ground.

Live attributes may change during retrieval. The UTC timestamp above records
this download, not when the City last updated every segment. Before reuse, review
`tbod_dataset_info("tampa-bike-lanes")$terms`, the linked ArcGIS item, and the
[City's conditions and use](https://www.tampa.gov/about-us/tampagov/conditions-and-use).
